rows.answer: The excerpts do not address exclusive dealing obligations or rights in the sense of restricting the Company or Agent from dealing with others. They state that the Agreement is the exclusive agreement among the parties and supersedes prior agreements, but that concerns the integration of the contract rather than exclusive dealing. The provided excerpts do not cover whether the Agent is the sole or exclusive agent for the offering.
The agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to principles of conflicts of law.

The excerpts do not state that either party may terminate without cause by simply giving notice. They describe the Agent's right to terminate under Section 12 based on specified events such as market disruption or a material adverse change, and the Company or Bank's right to terminate if the Agent is in material breach of Section 5 representations or covenants that remains uncured after notice. The excerpts provided do not address a general termination right without cause.

The excerpts provided do not address ownership of intellectual property created by either party. They cover the success fee, the Bank's corporate status and subsidiaries, title to real property and other assets, environmental law compliance, and capital stock ownership, but nothing about intellectual property created under the agreement.

Yes, but only in one direction: Bioamber has the right to audit Cargill's time sheets, once per year during reasonable business hours by an independent third party agreed to by both parties. The excerpts do not show a corresponding audit right for Cargill over Bioamber's records.
The agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Minnesota, United States of America, disregarding its conflicts of law rules.

The provided excerpts do not address whether the Development Agreement renews automatically or for how long. They refer to a Term defined in Section 10.1, but Section 10.1 is not included in the excerpts, so the renewal terms cannot be determined from them.

The excerpts do not establish a right to terminate without cause. Section 10.2 allows either party to terminate by written notice in cases of the other party's bankruptcy or insolvency, or a material default, and also upon mutual written agreement; these excerpts do not state a termination-for-convenience right based on notice alone.

Yes. The limitation on special, incidental, consequential, and punitive damages does not apply to liability for breach of the confidentiality obligations under Article 10, and it does not limit the parties' indemnification obligations under Article 12. The excerpts do not state that any other liability is unlimited.

Yes, neither party may recover special, incidental, consequential, or punitive damages from the other in connection with the agreement or any license granted under it. This limitation does not apply to liability for breach of confidentiality obligations under Article 10, nor does it limit the parties' indemnification obligations under Article 12.

The excerpts provided do not address whether either party has a right to audit the other's books or records. The excerpts cover an option to license an assay, existing technology and ownership, third-party infringement, confidentiality exceptions, and termination rights, but nothing on audits.

The excerpts do not discuss renewal of the agreement, so they do not say whether it renews or what notice is needed to prevent renewal. They do describe termination: either party may terminate for convenience on one hundred twenty (120) days written notice, and for a Change of Control Event the other party may terminate on thirty (30) days written notice. This is not legal advice.

Either Party must serve written notice of termination on the other at least 65 days before the end of the Initial Term, or any subsequent extension, to stop the contract from renewing. Notice served with less than the required period of notice is invalid and of no effect.
No. The contract states that neither Party may assign any of its rights or duties to third parties without the written consent of the other Party.

The excerpts do not state any cap or limit on either party's liability for damages. Section 8.1 says the parties are liable for non-execution or improper execution of their obligations under the legislation of the Republic of Kazakstan, and section 8.2 allocates liability for certain violations to the Principal, but neither sets a monetary or other limit on damages.

The excerpts provided do not address intellectual property ownership. They cover the parties, delivery and document obligations, the Company's fee and payment terms, confidentiality, and third-party rights, but say nothing about who owns intellectual property created under the contract.

The excerpts do not address limitation or exclusion of liability, so they do not say whether any claims have unlimited liability. The provided sections only introduce the Customization Schedule and describe the Customizations' specification requirements.

The excerpts do not address whether either party may terminate without cause by giving notice. The only termination right they describe is Bank of America's right to terminate this Schedule if Supplier increases the proposed price, with a refund of amounts previously paid.

Yes, as to the Sponsor. The Sponsor is not liable for errors of judgment, mistakes of law, or acts or omissions in overseeing, administering, or managing the Trust, except for willful misfeasance, bad faith, gross negligence, or reckless disregard of its obligations and duties. The excerpts do not state any limitation on the Trust's liability.
This agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, without reference to principles of conflicts of law.

The excerpts do not state whether the agreement renews automatically or for what term. They describe when the agreement takes effect and how it may be terminated or amended, but say nothing about renewal periods.

The excerpts provided do not address what happens if a party undergoes a change of control or is acquired. They cover the Sponsor's duties, its compensation, severability, and notice addresses, but say nothing about changes of control or acquisitions.

Not for both parties. The excerpts state that Dragon may terminate without cause by giving sixty days written notice to MMI, but they do not provide a without-cause termination right for MMI. Both parties may terminate immediately in specified circumstances such as material breach, merger or change of control, or bankruptcy.

The excerpts limit MMI's liability for indirect or consequential damages, unless they were caused by intention or gross negligence. They do not state a general monetary cap on either party's liability, and the liability clause only excuses failure or delay in performance for reasons beyond a party's reasonable control.

The excerpts do not state a general cap on liability or expressly say that liability is unlimited. They do state that MMI is not liable for indirect or consequential damages unless caused by intention or gross negligence, and that Dragon Systems may rescind or refuse payment notwithstanding any damage claims, but they do not establish whether any category of claim is unlimited in amount.

The excerpts do not address whether either party has the right to audit the other's books or records. The provided sections cover acceptance of services, invoicing and payment, liability, patents and copyright, and termination, but none mention audit rights.

No, not without the other party's consent. Section 11.2 bars either party from transferring or assigning its rights or delegating its obligations without the prior written consent of the other party, which may be withheld in that party's reasonable business discretion. The one exception is that, in connection with a merger, sale or transfer of substantially all of the assets or stock of one party, that party may provide for the assignee to be bound by the agreement's terms.

Yes. The liability cap of £200,000 does not apply to breaches of Section 8, and the exclusion of special and consequential damages also does not apply to breaches of Section 8. The excerpts do not show what Section 8 covers, so the scope of unlimited liability cannot be determined from them. The cap also excludes claims for monies due.

Yes. Section 4.5 requires each Party to retain its financial records relating to payments owed or paid under the Agreement for six years, but the excerpts do not expressly grant the other Party a right to inspect those records. The clause is titled "Audits," and the retention obligation is the only operative language provided in the excerpts.

The excerpts do not provide a termination-for-convenience clause allowing either party to terminate without cause. They do address termination for cause (material uncured breach, 6.2.1, with cure periods of 30 or 45 days), termination on bankruptcy or insolvency (6.2.2), and termination for contesting intellectual property rights (6.2.3). They also state that the Agreement runs for an initial three-year term and renews automatically for one-year terms unless either party gives notice of intent to terminate 90 days before the end of the current term, but that non-renewal notice is not the same as a termination without cause at any time.

No. HealthGate may not transfer or assign the agreement, in whole or in part, without the Publishers' prior written consent. The excerpts do not state whether the Publishers may assign without HealthGate's consent.

The excerpts do not contain a non-compete clause restricting either party from competing with the other. They only restrict Publishers from using Proprietary Software or Source Code held in escrow to develop a product that competes with HealthGate's services.

The excerpts do not provide a general right for either party to terminate without cause. They only describe termination on specific events, such as a change in control (Clause 32.2.2), the Publishers' right to terminate the licence in Clause 10.2.3 on three months' notice, and termination after a failure to complete the System (Clause 5.2). The excerpts do not cover a general no-cause termination right.

The excerpts do not state whether any claims have unlimited liability. They include indemnity provisions (Sections 28.1(a) and 28.1(b)) and a section titled 'Limitation of Liability' (Section 28), but the text of the limitation of liability provisions themselves is not included in the excerpts, so it cannot be determined from these excerpts whether any liability is unlimited.

Yes. Under Section 5.3, either Party may terminate the Agreement for any reason upon thirty (30) days' written notice to the other Party, unless that Party is itself a Defaulting Party under the Agreement.
No. The agreement states that no party may assign it without the prior written consent of the other party.

The excerpts do not address whether liability is limited or unlimited for any claims. They include a no-damages provision for decisions not to pursue a Project (Section 2.4) and a statement that neither Party is liable for the other's debts (Section 7.1), but no provision setting out a liability cap or stating that liability is unlimited.

The excerpts provided do not contain any exclusive dealing provisions. They cover survival of confidentiality obligations, events of default and remedies, notices, no partnership or agency, entire agreement, severability, and no third-party beneficiaries, but nothing addressing exclusive dealing obligations or rights.
The provided excerpts do not state which jurisdiction's law governs this agreement. They contain general compliance and separability provisions but no governing-law clause.

Yes. After the initial three-year term ends, the agreement automatically renews for an additional one-year term, unless a party gives written notice at least six months before the end of the initial term. During a renewed term, any party may terminate on six months' prior notice.

The agreement states that the Strategic Alliance is non-exclusive, so it does not create exclusive dealing obligations or rights for the Covered Businesses. The only exclusivity mentioned is an exclusive jurisdiction clause for court proceedings, which is a forum selection provision rather than an exclusive dealing arrangement.

The excerpts do not state whether liability is capped or unlimited for any claim. They describe Moelis Holdings' indemnification obligations for registration-related Losses (excluding consequential damages) and the Indemnifying Party's liability for settlements, but do not set out any overall liability cap or expressly state that liability is unlimited.

The excerpts do not state a non-renewal notice period or any automatic renewal provision. They cover the Initial Term (through the in-service date plus fifteen years) and termination for prolonged force majeure, which requires a Termination Notice at least twelve months before the Force Majeure Period expires, but they do not address renewal.

Yes, the contract allows either party to end it without stating a cause, but only by written notice given at least six months before the end of the Initial Term or the current Extension Period. The excerpts do not show a separate general right to terminate at any time without regard to the term, so the notice timing appears to be the operative condition.

The excerpts provided do not address exclusive dealing obligations or rights. They cover confidential information, definitions of Product and other terms, renewal and open season provisions, confidentiality disclosure, and assignment, but do not contain any exclusivity provision.

The excerpts provided do not address ownership of intellectual property created by either party. They define Confidential Information but do not state who owns intellectual property created under the agreement.

The excerpts state that Licensor is the sole owner of the Brand as between the parties, and that Licensee must not do anything inconsistent with that ownership. The excerpts do not address ownership of any other intellectual property created by either party, so they do not answer whether such property transfers to the other party.

No. Licensee may not assign, transfer, pledge, mortgage or otherwise encumber the agreement without Licensor's prior written consent in its sole discretion, with a narrow exception for an assignment outside bankruptcy to a successor organization that results solely from a name change. Any attempted assignment in violation is void and results in immediate termination.

The excerpts provided cover the term and termination provisions of the Trademark License Agreement but do not contain any non-compete or restriction on either party competing with the other. The contract does not address that question in the excerpts given.

The agreement does not renew in the usual sense because it has no fixed term to renew; it commences on the Effective Date and continues in perpetuity unless terminated under specified sections. Termination can occur for convenience by the Licensor, for uncured material breach, or automatically if the advisory relationship ends.

The excerpts do not address change of control or acquisition of a party as such. They contain a right of first refusal in Section 15.11, which applies when Licensor or its stockholder receives a bona fide offer to sell, transfer, or convey all or any stock in, or assets of, Licensor, but the excerpts do not state what happens in a general change of control or merger scenario.

Either party can stop the agreement from renewing by delivering written notice of termination to the other party at least sixty (60) days before the end of the original term or any renewal term. The agreement otherwise renews automatically for successive one-year terms.
The provided excerpts do not address ownership of intellectual property created by either party, so the contract as excerpted does not answer whether such property transfers to the other party.

The excerpts provided do not address whether either party has the right to audit the other's books or records. The provided sections cover the term and renewal, termination provisions, a right of first refusal, an option to purchase, and miscellaneous provisions, but nothing on audit rights.

No, not without the other party's consent. The agreement requires written consent for assignment or transfer to any person or entity, and any assignment made in violation of this is void. Consent is not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed, but withholding consent for an assignment to a competitor of the other party is deemed reasonable.

Yes. Section 11 excludes indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages and lost profits, revenue, data or use for either party, and caps E.piphany's liability at the total payments HSNS made under the initial term. Section 12.4 also bars either party from liability for loss of prospective profits or anticipated sales upon termination. The cap is stated only for E.piphany, not for HSNS.

The excerpts do not contain any exclusive dealing obligations or rights. They include provisions on reporting, warranties, ownership of deliverables, proprietary rights, survival, governing law, and fees, but nothing addressing exclusive dealing, and the excerpts are incomplete, so the rest of the contract is not available to confirm this.

The excerpts do not contain a non-compete or restriction on either party competing with the other. They address trademark use (Section 8.3), which bars confusing use of the other party's marks and challenges to them, but that is not a general restriction on competition.
No. The agreement states that no party may transfer or assign its rights or obligations without the prior written consent of the other parties, and any assignment in contravention is void.

The excerpts do not address exclusive dealing obligations or rights. They cover the Corporation's representations and warranties, intellectual property representations, closing conditions, termination rights, remedies, severability, and expenses, but contain no exclusivity provision.

The provided excerpts do not address whether the agreement renews automatically or for how long; they only contain representations and warranties of the Corporation regarding its corporate status, financial statements, intellectual property, labour matters and securities liability.

The excerpts do not contain a general limit on either party's liability for damages. They do contain an exclusion of certain damages in the Corporation's indemnity to the Agents, which excludes loss of profits and consequential or punitive damages from the indemnified losses, but this is not a cap on liability for damages overall. The excerpts do not address whether the Agents' own liability to the Corporation is capped.

Yes. The agreement grants The Henry Film and Entertainment Corporation a 10 year exclusive, worldwide license to use Pacificap Entertainment's nostalgic television show library content. The excerpts also refer to a 10 year Exclusive Content License granted in lieu of a minimum annual performance payment.
Either party can stop the agreement from automatically renewing by giving notice to the other party not less than sixty (60) days before the end of a Term.

The excerpts provided do not address whether either party may assign this agreement, so they do not say whether assignment without the other party's consent is permitted. No citations are given because no excerpt covers assignment.

The excerpts provided do not address whether either party has a right to audit the other party's books or records. The excerpts cover content redistribution, indemnification, term and termination, ownership of brand features, and dispute resolution, but none mention audit rights.

Yes, the Member (not the Franchisor) is restricted from competing. During the term of the Franchise Agreement, the Member may not have an interest in a business that operates a restaurant featuring pizza and related food specialties or offers substantially similar products or services. For a two-year Post-Term Period, the Member may not have an interest in a Competitive Business within a three-mile radius of the Franchised Business premises or of any Franchised Business operating or under construction under the System.

The excerpts do not address whether either party may assign this agreement or what consent would be required for an assignment. The excerpts only reference a transfer under Section 14 of the Franchise Agreement, which is not included in the provided text.

The excerpts do not address renewal of the agreement or any notice period needed to stop renewal. They cover confidentiality, non-competition covenants, injunctive relief, severability, delay/waiver, and third-party beneficiary terms, but say nothing about automatic renewal.
The agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York, except for matters directly within the purview of the DGCL, which are governed by the DGCL (Delaware General Corporation Law).

The excerpts do not contain a general termination-for-convenience clause allowing either party to terminate the agreement without cause by giving notice. They address termination of the Farids Group's board nomination right (tied to share ownership and EA Revenue thresholds) and withdrawal of a proposed registration, but not termination of the agreement itself.

The excerpts do not address any automatic renewal or termination of the agreement, so they do not state how much notice is needed to stop it from renewing. The provided sections only cover piggyback registration rights, custody agreements, and related notice requirements for registration statements and share sales.

The excerpts do not contain a general limit on either party's liability for damages. They do include an indemnification contribution cap, which limits a Holder's contribution to the net proceeds from the registered offering, but they do not address a general cap on liability.

The excerpts do not address automatic renewal or how much notice is required to stop the agreement from renewing. They only cover termination following a dispute over economic adjustments (Section 8.3 language) and termination for uncured Carrier Default under Section 8.4.
The provided excerpts do not contain any term or renewal provision, so they do not say whether this agreement renews automatically or for how long.

The excerpts do not contain any exclusive dealing provisions. They address carrier and shipper rights, tariff compliance, remedies, dispute resolution, third-party beneficiaries, and the independent contractor status of the parties, but none of the provided sections state whether either party must deal exclusively with the other.

The provided excerpts do not address intellectual property ownership, including whether IP created by one party becomes owned by the other. The contract excerpts cover definitions of plants, losses, product quality specifications, off-spec penalties, and nomination requirements, but nothing on intellectual property.

The agreement continues in effect for one year from its execution date and then from year to year thereafter, but only if the continuance is specifically approved by a majority of the Non-Interested Trustees. It therefore does not renew purely automatically; it requires that trustee approval each year.

The excerpts provided do not address whether either party has a right to audit the other's books or records. They cover the Net Investment Income maintenance commitment, the definition of Fund Investment Income, the Investment Adviser's right of recovery of expense waivers, and the agreement's term and termination.

The excerpts do not address exclusive dealing. They cover the Investment Adviser's obligation to maintain the Fund's net investment income, the Underwriter's possible waiver of Rule 12b-1 fees with reimbursement rights, term and termination, and definitions, but nothing about exclusivity obligations or rights.

The agreement is governed by the laws of China. Disputes arising from its interpretation and performance are to be negotiated first and, failing agreement within 30 days, may be submitted to the Beijing Arbitration Commission.

Generally no: neither party may assign or transfer its rights and obligations, in whole or in part, without the prior written consent of the other party. However, Party A may transfer its rights and obligations to any of its Affiliates without that consent, provided it gives written notice to Party B.

Yes. The agreement provides that Party A (Didi Chuxing Technology Co., Ltd.) has exclusive rights and interests in all rights, ownership, titles, interests and intellectual property rights arising from or created by the performance of the agreement, so intellectual property created through performance vests in Party A rather than Party B.

The excerpts do not contain an express right for either party to audit the other's books or records. They do mention that Party A may investigate Party B's background and that Party B must actively cooperate in the audit of Didi Chuxing, but they do not establish a general books-and-records audit right.

The excerpts do not contain a limitation of liability clause capping either party's liability for damages. They describe the Customer's liability for User Activity and Reversals, including a Reversal Fee and collection rights, but do not state any cap on damages.

The excerpts do not address a change of control or acquisition of either party. They cover termination for material breach, untrue representations, bankruptcy or insolvency, changes in law, regulatory direction, material adverse change in financial condition, and prolonged force majeure, but none of these mention a change of control or acquisition.

No. Section S54 states that neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under it to a third party without the written consent of the other party. Section S10 separately bars Sparkling from assigning the Agreement or transferring the Work except as authorized in writing by Garman.

Sparkling may terminate the Agreement at any time without cause on ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. The excerpts do not state an equivalent without-cause termination right for Garman, so they do not confirm that either party can terminate in that way.

The excerpts provided do not address whether either party has a right to audit the other's books or records. They cover software acceptance, support services, infringement remedies, and confidentiality, but contain no audit provision.

The excerpts state that Garman owns all intellectual property rights in the Work, including any Improvements or Modifications, and that no title to that intellectual property is transferred to Sparkling by the Agreement. The excerpts do not address ownership of intellectual property created by Sparkling, so they do not answer whether such property would become owned by Garman.
This agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Minnesota, without giving effect to conflict of laws principles.

The excerpts do not state a cap or limit on either party's liability for damages. They describe liquidated damages owed by the Investor, measured by the lesser of unpaid Required Capital Contributions and the outstanding Obligations, but they do not establish a general limit on liability for either party.

The excerpts do not contain a provision allowing either party to terminate the Agreement without cause by giving notice. They describe a continuing agreement that remains in effect until the Obligations are paid in full and commitments are terminated, and a Release Request process for the Investor that is subject to conditions not fully shown in the excerpts.

The excerpts do not address exclusive dealing. They cover specific performance and liquidated damages, capital contributions to a Special Account, unconditional obligations, events of default, jury waiver, and continuing agreement terms, but nothing about exclusive dealing obligations or rights.

The excerpts do not address whether either party is restricted from competing with the other. They contain only the signature page and an effectiveness clause that amends an existing Reseller Agreement dated August 1, 2015, which is not provided.

The excerpts do not address renewal or non-renewal of the agreement, so they do not state how much notice is needed to stop it from renewing. The excerpts only cover the sub-reseller appointment, the effect of the sub-reseller agreement on the underlying Reseller Agreement, entire agreement, and counterparts.

No. Under Article VII, the rights and obligations may not be assigned by Company without first obtaining BP's written consent, and any assignment without BP's consent is voidable by BP. The excerpts do not state whether BP may assign without Company's consent.

The agreement is governed by and construed under the laws of the State of Louisiana, except to the extent Louisiana's conflict of law rules would require another state's laws to govern its validity, construction, or interpretation.

The excerpts do not contain an automatic renewal provision. They state the term: Section 6.1 provides that the Agreement terminates one year from the Rig Release Date (unless Sections 6.2-6.5 apply), and Sections 6.2 and 6.3 extend the Agreement's duration while an Operating Agreement remains in effect or while Company participates in a Substitute Well. These are extensions tied to specific events rather than an automatic renewal, and the excerpts do not describe any renewal term.

The excerpts do not state whether any claims carry unlimited liability. They include a limitation of BP's liability to losses resulting from gross negligence or willful misconduct, and a waiver of Company's claims against BP Group regarding certain property matters, but they do not address whether liability for any other claims is unlimited or what the full scope of liability limits is.

Yes, the excerpts show that VS must make its records available to PPD for examination. Section 15 requires VS to cooperate with internal reviews or audits by PPD or Sponsor and to make available for examination and duplication all documentation, data and information relating to the Agreement or any Work Order. The excerpts do not describe any reciprocal audit right for VS over PPD's records.

Yes, in part. Unless otherwise addressed in an Intellectual Property Amendment, VS assigns to PPD (or the Sponsor) rights in intellectual property developed using Confidential Information provided by PPD, and PPD assigns to VS rights in intellectual property developed using Confidential Information provided by VS. Ownership of property resulting from development of a Joint Solution is to be addressed by separate written agreement.

Yes, in part. Section 3(a)(v) restricts VS from entering the same or substantially similar Commitments with any PPD Competitor performing similar clinical research services, and from giving such a competitor better pricing; PPD is likewise barred from entering substantially similar commitments with any other imaging vendor for Preferred Services. The excerpts do not show a general non-compete beyond these commitment restrictions, and the Covenant Not to Interfere in Section 21 concerns soliciting employees only.

Yes. BOSCH grants CLIENT exclusive distribution rights to sell and distribute the Products in the Territory (the United States and Canada, excluding the US Virgin Islands), but the exclusivity is limited to select companies in the Automotive Industry, each approved by BOSCH in writing on a case-by-case basis. The agreement also says CLIENT will not authorize any other party to take actions that would derogate from, impair or compete with the Exclusive Rights, though BOSCH keeps reserved rights to its current clients and reserves the right to share rights unless it disrupts CLIENT's business.
The excerpts provided do not contain an assignment clause, so they do not address whether either party may assign this agreement without the other party's consent.

The excerpts do not contain a governing law or choice-of-law clause, so they do not state which jurisdiction's law governs this agreement. The parties' addresses are both in Nevada, but the excerpts do not say that Nevada law applies.

rows.answer: The excerpts do not contain an exclusive dealing obligation binding Manufacturer. Instead, Section 15.4 expressly allows Subcontractor to sell similar products to third parties, including competitors of Manufacturer, which indicates the arrangement is non-exclusive in that respect.
